$comment: Single source of truth for backup exclusions. Consumed by BOTH active archivers: src/infra/cli/commands/backup.ts (CLI + built-in 02:00 scheduler) and scripts/scheduled-backup-runner.mjs (systemd 04:00 timer). Adding a secret here must never mean editing two files — that asymmetry is the defect this file exists to remove.
$whyGlobs: tar --exclude matches glob patterns, not literal paths. The previous `--exclude=./vault-entries.json` excluded exactly one filename and missed `vault-entries.json.bak-diag-*`, which was measured present in 6/7 archives on this host. Secret excludes MUST use a trailing `*`.
$embedTmpNote: The semantic index is written atomically as `${file_name}.tmp-${pid}-${stamp}` and then renamed (crates/memphis-embed/src/pipeline.rs, unique_tmp_path). The current default file name is `index-v1.json`; `embed-index.json` is the legacy configured path (RUST_EMBED_PERSIST_PATH). Both temp forms are excluded, because both names can appear on disk — an interrupted write leaves the temp file behind.
$walNote: SQLite -wal/-shm are deliberately NOT excluded. Removing them from a copy of a live database yields a db that opens but silently lacks committed transactions; the correct approach is a consistent snapshot (sqlite backup API), not exclusion. Measured gap: data/memphis.db (30.6 MB) is absent from 7/7 archives because the runner only archives /home/memphis/.memphis.
$rootLevelNote: Every secret is listed twice: as `*/name` and as `name*`. The bare `*/name` glob needs a directory component in front of the name, so it does not match a secret stored at the archive root — measured on the macOS runner, where `./vault-state.json` came out inside the archive. The `name*` form matches at every level, root included, on both GNU tar and the BSD tar on macOS.
